strategy.summary: Reproduce the mid-range and large-n Generator.binomial defect in numba's random_binomial_btpe at the buggy commit 30c17f24486c, then confirm the developer's test_binomial_specific_issues fails there and passes at the fixed revision. Build numba from source at the buggy commit with an era-inferred NumPy 1.24 and Python 3.10. Run the test under a hard timeout, because the n=700 subtest may hang on the buggy revision rather than fail.

pinned_because: numba is pinned to the buggy commit 30c17f24486c, which is the revision under test, so this pin is documented by the checkout itself rather than inferred

numpy 1.24.4 is era-inferred and not documented: issue #9493 names only numba 0.59 and no numpy version, so 1.24 is chosen as a plausible NumPy of the numba 0.59 era; this is not a documented constraint
llvmlite is era-inferred to match numba 0.59 at this commit; the evidence gives no llvmlite constraint

strategy.test_command: timeout 600 python -m pytest numba/tests/test_np_randomgen.py -k test_binomial_specific_issues -v -p no:cacheprovider
strategy.reproducing_test: numba/tests/test_np_randomgen.py::test_binomial_specific_issues (added in PR #9747; two subtests: 'infinite loop issue #9493' with binomial(700,0.1,100) and 'issue with midrange value branch #9493/#9734' with binomial(301,0.1,100))
strategy.success_criterion: Transition: on the buggy revision 30c17f24486c, the test fails, either as an assertPreciseEqual mismatch in the mid-range subtest (jitted and py_func arrays differ) or as a hang in the n=700 subtest that the timeout kills and counts as a failure; on the fixed revision the test completes and both subtests pass with assertPreciseEqual.
strategy.numerical_probe: Seeded comparison: foo=numba.jit of lambda g: g.binomial(301,0.1,3) run on default_rng(0) versus foo.py_func on a second default_rng(0); buggy path differs from py_func, fixed path agrees.

input_output_examples.input: gen.binomial(301, 0.1, 3) with gen = np.random.default_rng(0), jitted via @jit, compared against foo.py_func(default_rng(0))

risks: The hang on n=700 may not terminate on the buggy revision; the test must run under a timeout (the command uses timeout 600) and a killed run must be read as a failure, not a pass.

Reproduction depends on the default_rng(0) stream and the NumPy version used for the py_func reference; a different NumPy release may change the reference values, so the mismatch may shift even though the defect remains.
The issue reports the bug only with default_rng(0) on the author's machine; other seeds or platforms may not trigger the mid-range deviation, so the transition is not guaranteed elsewhere.
The NumPy version is era-inferred, not documented; if the chosen NumPy 1.24.4 is incompatible with the buggy commit's build, the reference path could differ or fail to build.
The defect comes from an int cast on a floating-point value in a branch-dependent algorithm; if the platform's libm or float rounding differs, the threshold behaviour may not appear identically.
The test class containing test_binomial_specific_issues was not named in the evidence, so the test command selects by -k name rather than by class path.

oracle.reference_source: NumPy Generator.binomial via the py_func path, which follows numpy/random/src/distributions/distributions.c (fall-through near lines 752-754, binomial near line 635)
oracle.why: The outputs are integer count arrays, so the comparison is exact equality through assertPreciseEqual with no tolerance.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision the mid-range subtest sees the jitted array [33, 31, 23] against the py_func array [32, 31, 22], so assertPreciseEqual raises AssertionError; the n=700 subtest may instead loop forever in the missing fall-through branch, so the timeout kills it and the run counts as a failure.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the int cast on p1 is removed and the fall-through to case=60 is added, so both subtests terminate and the jitted and py_func arrays match exactly, letting the test pass.
